name: Woolhead Sculpin
imitates: A bottom-hugging sculpin; the wool head soaks up water and sinks, so it earns its place crawled slowly along riffles and deep pools on a sink-tip.

steps.text: Wrap about twenty turns of lead wire on the shank, leaving the front quarter bare, then lay a thread base over it back to the bend.
Tie in the rib wire at the back of the lead and dub a thick, shaggy, slightly tapered body up to the front of the lead wraps.
Tie the rabbit strip in at the front of the body, catching only the tip of the hide so it does not build bulk. Trim the hide end to a taper first.
Part the fur above the barb and counter-wrap the wire forward in evenly spaced turns, parting the fur for each turn, to lock the strip down Matuka style. Tie off and stroke the fur back.
Flip the hook, comb out a clump of red wool and tie it under the shank at the front of the body as a throat that reaches just short of the hook point.
Build a thread base to the eye. Tie in a large clump of olive wool at the front of the body, letting it wrap 360 degrees around the shank, and pack it back.
Add a second clump of olive wool (butt ends only) at the front edge of the first, bind it down tightly and pull the thread to the front.
Brush the very bushy head out with a bodkin or dubbing brush to free loose fibers.
Trim the head flat across the bottom (without cutting the red throat) and across the top, then round the sides so the head flows into the wing as a teardrop.
Finished fly: wide, flat wool head, red throat showing underneath, and the rabbit strip trailing about two shank lengths behind.
